notes: Revenue has compounded 43.8% a year over five years.
EBITDA margin widened: -23.0% in FY21 to 33.0% in FY26.
Growth is slowing: 18.6% a year over three years against 43.8% over five.
Borrowings ₹3,471 cr against net worth ₹13,640 cr: debt/equity 0.25, lightly geared.
Borrowings fell from ₹5,518 cr in FY21.
Working-capital days stretched from -555 to -37 over 5 years.
Over 5 years, operating cash flow was 139% of reported profit: profits are turning into cash.

business.what_it_does: The Indian Hotels Company Limited operates a hospitality ecosystem, selling accommodation, dining, wellness, and catering services to business and leisure travellers. It generates revenue through hotel operations, management contracts, culinary services, and fee-based lifestyle and experiential platforms.
other_facts: IHCL has a portfolio of 630 hotels including a pipeline of 255 hotels across 15 countries.
The company operates over 33,000 hotel rooms (keys) globally.
Tata Neu loyalty programme serves over 16 million members.

ledger.credibility: Management demonstrates mixed reliability. They successfully deliver core revenue and capex guidance, such as achieving 16.3% revenue growth and Rs. 1,000 crores capex in FY26. However, they frequently drop or stop mentioning specific portfolio and expansion targets.
bull: Revenue compounded at a strong 43.8% annually over five years, reaching a TTM revenue of ₹10,431 cr.
EBITDA margin has widened significantly from -23.0% in FY21 to 33.0% in FY26.
Balance sheet is lightly geared with borrowings at ₹3,471 cr against net worth of ₹13,640 cr (debt/equity 0.25).
bear: Growth is slowing down noticeably, dropping to 18.6% annually over three years compared to 43.8% over five years.
Valuation appears demanding with a P/E ratio of 63.0 against an ROE of 15.4% and ROCE of 17.1%.
Working-capital days have stretched considerably from -555 days to -37 days over the five-year period.
